## Version 2.0: Generic rework - automatic plate detection, generic metadata columns, separate OM data - 08.10.2026 | JM
## Version 1.1: Updated version log format - 17.07.2025 | JM
## Version 1.0: EEA raw data processing routine - 11.02.2025 | JM
## Purpose: Process raw plate reader files of fluorometric hydrolase assays into enzyme activities per sample

# Step 1: Prepare session
## Step 1a: Install necessary packages
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#install.packages("here")
#install.packages("readxl")
#install.packages("tidyverse")
```

## Step 1b: Load necessary packages
```{r, message=FALSE}
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
```

## Step 1c: Define settings
```{r}
# Folders and files
path_raw       <- here("data", "hydrolases", "raw")
path_metadata  <- here("data", "hydrolases", "metadata", "df_hydrolases_metadata.xlsx")
path_om        <- here("data", "om", "df_om.xlsx")
path_processed <- here("data", "hydrolases", "processed")

# Assay constants
standard_nmol   <- 5      # Amount of fluorescent standard per well [nmol]
homogenate_ml   <- 0.2    # Volume of sample homogenate per well [mL]
max_activity_om <- 10000  # Upper plausibility limit for activity_om [nmol g OM-1 h-1]
```

# Step 2: Load data
## Step 2a: Load metadata
```{r}
# One row per sample on a plate
df_hydrolases_0_metadata <- read_excel(path_metadata) %>%
  mutate(
    id            = as.character(id),
    sampling_date = as_date(sampling_date)
  )

df_hydrolases_0_metadata
```

## Step 2b: Load OM data
```{r}
# One row per sample with the crucible weights of the loss-on-ignition measurement
df_om_0_raw <- read_excel(path_om) %>%
  mutate(id = as.character(id))

df_om_0_raw
```

## Step 2c: Load raw plate reader data
```{r}
# Every .csv file in the raw folder is one plate
plate_files <- list.files(path_raw, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)

# Read all plates into one table: one line per plate row, columns col_1 to col_12
df_hydrolases_1_raw <- read_csv(
  plate_files,
  id             = "file",
  skip           = 1,
  col_names      = paste0("col_", 1:12),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Plate name = file name without ".csv"; row = plate row 1 to 8
df_hydrolases_1_raw <- df_hydrolases_1_raw %>%
  mutate(plate = str_remove(basename(file), fixed(".csv"))) %>%
  group_by(plate) %>%
  mutate(row = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(plate, row, col_1:col_12)

df_hydrolases_1_raw
```

# Step 3: Assign wells to samples
## Step 3a: Split plates by sample position
```{r}
# Plate layout - each plate row is one technical replicate:
#
#              col 1-3      col 4-6      col 7-9      col 10-12
#   rows 1-4   reference    position 1   position 2   position 3
#   rows 5-8   reference    position 4   position 5   position 6
#
# Reference columns: 1 = blank, 2 = standard, 3 = substrate control
# Sample columns:    1st = homogenate control, 2nd = quench, 3rd = assay

df_position_1 <- df_hydrolases_1_raw %>%
  filter(row %in% 1:4) %>%
  select(plate, row,
         blank = col_1, standard = col_2, substrate_control = col_3,
         homogenate_control = col_4, quench = col_5, assay = col_6) %>%
  mutate(position = 1)

df_position_2 <- df_hydrolases_1_raw %>%
  filter(row %in% 1:4) %>%
  select(plate, row,
         blank = col_1, standard = col_2, substrate_control = col_3,
         homogenate_control = col_7, quench = col_8, assay = col_9) %>%
  mutate(position = 2)

df_position_3 <- df_hydrolases_1_raw %>%
  filter(row %in% 1:4) %>%
  select(plate, row,
         blank = col_1, standard = col_2, substrate_control = col_3,
         homogenate_control = col_10, quench = col_11, assay = col_12) %>%
  mutate(position = 3)

df_position_4 <- df_hydrolases_1_raw %>%
  filter(row %in% 5:8) %>%
  select(plate, row,
         blank = col_1, standard = col_2, substrate_control = col_3,
         homogenate_control = col_4, quench = col_5, assay = col_6) %>%
  mutate(position = 4)

df_position_5 <- df_hydrolases_1_raw %>%
  filter(row %in% 5:8) %>%
  select(plate, row,
         blank = col_1, standard = col_2, substrate_control = col_3,
         homogenate_control = col_7, quench = col_8, assay = col_9) %>%
  mutate(position = 5)

df_position_6 <- df_hydrolases_1_raw %>%
  filter(row %in% 5:8) %>%
  select(plate, row,
         blank = col_1, standard = col_2, substrate_control = col_3,
         homogenate_control = col_10, quench = col_11, assay = col_12) %>%
  mutate(position = 6)

# Combine all positions: one line per well row of a sample
df_hydrolases_2_wells <- bind_rows(
  df_position_1, df_position_2, df_position_3,
  df_position_4, df_position_5, df_position_6
)

df_hydrolases_2_wells
```

## Step 3b: Average technical replicates
```{r}
# Mean of the four technical replicates per sample
df_hydrolases_3_means <- df_hydrolases_2_wells %>%
  group_by(plate, position) %>%
  summarise(
    n_replicates       = n(),
    blank              = mean(blank, na.rm = TRUE),
    standard           = mean(standard, na.rm = TRUE),
    substrate_control  = mean(substrate_control, na.rm = TRUE),
    homogenate_control = mean(homogenate_control, na.rm = TRUE),
    quench             = mean(quench, na.rm = TRUE),
    assay              = mean(assay, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

df_hydrolases_3_means
```

# Step 4: Calculate enzyme activities
## Step 4a: Calculate dry matter and OM fractions
```{r}
# All fractions refer to the fresh sample, like the sample mass of the assay
df_om_1_fractions <- df_om_0_raw %>%
  mutate(
    fw_g        = crucible_fw - crucible_weight,       # Fresh sample
    dw_g        = crucible_dw_105 - crucible_weight,   # Dry sample after 105 °C
    om_g        = crucible_dw_105 - crucible_loi_550,  # Organic matter lost at 550 °C
    dw_fraction = dw_g / fw_g,
    om_fraction = om_g / fw_g
  )

# Show implausible fractions (outside 0-1), e.g. typos in the crucible weights
df_om_1_fractions %>%
  filter(dw_fraction < 0 | dw_fraction > 1 | om_fraction < 0 | om_fraction > 1)

# Set implausible fractions to NA
df_om_2_checked <- df_om_1_fractions %>%
  mutate(
    dw_fraction = if_else(dw_fraction < 0 | dw_fraction > 1, NA, dw_fraction),
    om_fraction = if_else(om_fraction < 0 | om_fraction > 1, NA, om_fraction)
  ) %>%
  select(id, dw_fraction, om_fraction)
```

## Step 4b: Check that metadata, raw data and OM data match
```{r}
# Each check shows the problematic lines - an empty table means everything is fine

# Check 1: plate positions listed twice in the metadata
df_hydrolases_0_metadata %>%
  count(plate, position) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

# Check 2: samples listed twice in the OM data
df_om_0_raw %>%
  count(id) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

# Check 3: plates in the raw folder without metadata (these are not processed)
df_hydrolases_3_means %>%
  distinct(plate) %>%
  anti_join(df_hydrolases_0_metadata, by = "plate")

# Check 4: samples in the metadata without raw data
df_hydrolases_0_metadata %>%
  anti_join(df_hydrolases_3_means, by = c("plate", "position"))

# Check 5: samples in the metadata without OM data
df_hydrolases_0_metadata %>%
  anti_join(df_om_0_raw, by = "id")
```

## Step 4c: Merge metadata, fluorescence and OM data
```{r}
df_hydrolases_4_merged <- df_hydrolases_0_metadata %>%
  left_join(df_hydrolases_3_means, by = c("plate", "position")) %>%
  left_join(df_om_2_checked, by = "id")
```

## Step 4d: Calculate activities
```{r}
df_hydrolases_5_activity <- df_hydrolases_4_merged %>%
  mutate(
    # Incubation time [h]
    incubation_h = as.numeric(difftime(incubation_end, incubation_start, units = "hours")),

    # Fluorescence per nmol of standard
    emission_coef = standard / standard_nmol,

    # Change of the standard fluorescence by the sample (quenching)
    quench_coef = (quench - homogenate_control) / standard,

    # Fluorescence produced by the enzyme
    net_fluorescence = (assay - homogenate_control) / quench_coef - substrate_control,

    # Activity per g fresh sample, dry sample and organic matter [nmol g-1 h-1]
    activity_fw = (net_fluorescence * buffer_ml) /
                  (emission_coef * homogenate_ml * incubation_h * sample_g),
    activity_dw = activity_fw / dw_fraction,
    activity_om = activity_fw / om_fraction
  )
```

## Step 4e: Quality control
```{r}
# Samples are flagged instead of removed, so that every sample stays in the output
df_hydrolases_6_processed <- df_hydrolases_5_activity %>%
  mutate(
    qc_flag = case_when(
      is.na(activity_fw)            ~ "missing assay data",
      activity_fw <= 0              ~ "activity <= 0",
      activity_om > max_activity_om ~ "activity above limit",
      .default = "ok"
    )
  )

# Show all samples that did not pass the quality control
df_hydrolases_6_processed %>%
  filter(qc_flag != "ok") %>%
  select(id, plate, position, sample_g, buffer_ml, activity_fw, qc_flag)
```

# Step 5: Save processed data
```{r}
dir.create(path_processed, showWarnings = FALSE)

write_csv(df_hydrolases_6_processed,
          file.path(path_processed, "df_hydrolases_processed.csv"))
```

# Step 6: Summary of dataframes
```{r}
# Number of samples per enzyme and quality flag
df_hydrolases_6_processed %>%
  count(enzyme, qc_flag)

# Activities of the samples that passed the quality control
df_hydrolases_6_processed %>%
  filter(qc_flag == "ok") %>%
  select(activity_fw, activity_dw, activity_om) %>%
  summary()
```
